author: agent:claude-code
message: The user chose how Slurm shares vgsquid-jade between colleagues; Slurm on vgsquid-jade: a one-node cluster that gates the p150a and the CPUs between colleagues with fairshare, plus what's left to do on the machine (proposal 01a171dd-c051-7070-9749-e670df371f14, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: Slurm gates the p150a and the CPUs on vgsquid-jade
why: The user chose Slurm-gated access over an honor system: the card's device nodes stop being open to every user; a Slurm prolog grants the job's user access to the card it was allocated and the epilog takes it back and clears that user's files in /dev/hugepages-1G. Login sessions get a capped CPU/memory share (a systemd user-slice limit), so real work goes through sbatch/srun. Rejected: leaving /dev/tenstorrent/* 0666 with Slurm only scheduling (anyone can skip the queue), and pam_slurm_adopt (no shell without a running job, which on a one-node cluster is also where people submit from).

text: Fairshare priority with slurmdbd accounting on vgsquid-jade
why: The user chose fairshare with accounting over FIFO + backfill: slurmdbd on a local MariaDB (unix-socket auth, so no database password exists), multifactor priority weighted by fairshare, so heavy users drop in priority and sacct keeps per-user history. Each colleague needs a Slurm association (sacctmgr add user) alongside their guest account.

name: Slurm
intent: Slurm as a one-node cluster on a shared box: schedules cores, memory and Tenstorrent cards (the `tt` GRES) between the owner and core.headless.guests, with fairshare priority from slurmdbd accounting on a local MariaDB. Access is gated: cards are root-only outside a job, login sessions get a capped slice.

text: A card is usable only by the user of the job holding it
why: The user chose Slurm-gated access. A udev rule after tt-kmd's makes /dev/tenstorrent/* 0600 root; the prolog (PrologFlags=Alloc) reads the job's GRES indices from `scontrol show job -d` and adds the job user's ACL; the epilog removes it, kills whatever still holds the card (an fd outlives the ACL) and clears that user's /dev/hugepages-1G files unless another of their jobs runs. ConstrainDevices=yes keeps a job off cards it wasn't given.

text: Login sessions share a capped user.slice; jobs run outside it
why: So heavy work goes through Slurm: user.slice gets CPUQuota (modules.slurm.login.cpus) and MemoryMax (login.memory), as a drop-in; slurmd's jobs live under system.slice. MemSpecLimit keeps the login share, the cards' hugepages and 2 GiB for daemons out of what jobs can allocate. The owner's own sessions (GNOME included) are inside the cap too.

text: Every login account has a Slurm association, from the same list that makes the accounts
why: AccountingStorageEnforce=associations refuses jobs from users without one. The slurm-accounts oneshot adds the owner and every core.headless.guests name to the `colleagues` account, so adding a guest is one edit. It only adds: a removed guest keeps a stale association.

text: The munge key and slurmdbd's database password are made on the host at first boot, never in the store or the repo
why: Secrets never live in repos. munge-key creates /etc/munge/munge.key once (mungekey); slurmdbd-storage-pass writes a random /var/lib/slurmdbd/storage-pass once and sets it on MariaDB's slurm user (as root over the socket) before slurmdbd starts, via storagePassFile.

text: The node's hardware line comes from `slurmd -C` on the machine
why: A host's hardware is read where it lives: jade's is CPUs=24 Boards=1 SocketsPerBoard=1 CoresPerSocket=12 ThreadsPerCore=2 RealMemory=63432, from slurmd -C on jade. The module asserts modules.slurm.node is set.

title: Prolog named slurm.conf, which names the prolog: infinite recursion
body: The first prolog/epilog exported SLURM_CONF=${etcSlurm}/slurm.conf, but slurm.conf carries Prolog=/Epilog= store paths, so evaluation recursed. Lesson: scripts slurm.conf points at find the Slurm tools at run time (/run/current-system/sw/bin, the wrapped binaries that carry the config), never through etcSlurm or the wrappers' store paths.

title: Checked by building, not yet on the machine
body: Verified from vghydra under WSL: jade's etcSlurm builds (slurm.conf, cgroup.conf, gres.conf as intended), the prolog and epilog pass shellcheck, jade's whole system.build.etc builds, check-hosts.sh and exports.test.sh pass. Not verified: anything at run time (munge, MariaDB socket auth then password, slurmdbd, slurmd under cgroup v2, the ACL handoff, user.slice limits). No VM test: vgwsl2 has no /dev/kvm (graft 01a165ae) and flake checks don't exist yet.

title: Bring vgsquid-jade up: bootstrap, commit its hardware-configuration.nix, join the tailnet
body: On jade: git pull ~/vg-dotfiles, ./bootstrap.sh vgsquid-jade, commit the staged nix/nixos/vgsquid-jade/hardware-configuration.nix. Then `sudo tailscale up` (no --ssh: jade keeps Tailscale SSH off) and log in once in the browser. Add your own public key to core.headless.sshd.authorizedKeys on jade so password login turns off.

title: Onboard colleagues to vgsquid-jade
body: Per colleague: their ed25519 public key into core.headless.guests in nix/nixos/vgsquid-jade/default.nix (that also gives them a Slurm association), rebuild, then share the vgsquid-jade node to their email from the Tailscale admin console (Machines > vgsquid-jade > Share). They accept with their own Tailscale account and `ssh <name>@vgsquid-jade`. The first one confirms the node-share + OpenSSH path (the claim still says 'to verify with the first colleague').

title: Verify Slurm on vgsquid-jade after its first build
body: In a session on jade: systemctl status munged mysql slurmdbd slurmctld slurmd slurm-accounts munge-key slurmdbd-storage-pass; `sinfo -N -o '%N %T %c %m %G'` shows vgsquid-jade idle with tt:p150a:1; `sacctmgr show assoc format=cluster,account,user`; as a non-root user `ls -l /dev/tenstorrent/0` and `tt-smi -s` fails outside a job; `srun --gres=tt:1 -c4 --mem=8G tt-smi -s` works and `getfacl /dev/tenstorrent/0` shows that user only during the job; afterwards the ACL is gone; `systemctl show user.slice -p CPUQuotaPerSecUSec -p MemoryMax`; `sprio`/`sshare` show fairshare. If slurmd fails on cgroup v2, read `journalctl -u slurmd` before changing anything. Record what held and what didn't on NixOS/Slurm.

title: NixOS VM test for the Slurm module
body: A checks VM test with modules.tenstorrent off: services come up, a user without an association is refused, one with it runs sbatch, user.slice carries the caps. Needs KVM (CI's Linux runners) and flake checks.
